title: [factory-setup-agent] Setup round 1: sandbox designed and proven at build_and_test
body:
Setup phase 2, round 1. Everything is written to `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/setup/` for the trial to pick up: `manifest.json`, the four `context/` files, and `research-domains.txt`. No `stubs/` — nothing here talks to a third party.

`previous/` was empty, so this is the first round.

## What this repo is

A pure Ruby library, and nothing else. `lib/scheduling/` holds two classes — `Slot` (a half-open time range) and `Calendar` (one room's bookings, raising `Calendar::Conflict` rather than returning false) — in 75 lines, with a 50-line minitest suite. There is **no app**: no `bin/`, no `exe/`, no server, no CLI entry point, no gemspec. Nothing in `lib/` or `test/` reads an environment variable, opens a file or socket, or contacts a database or third party.

So: `env`, `services` and `stubs` are all empty, `run` and `app_url` are null, and no credential of anyone's is involved anywhere.

## Claim

**`tier: build_and_test`** — the ceiling the repo allows, since there is no process to start.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| install | `bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle && bundle install`, behind a PATH prefix (below) |
| build | `null` — a Ruby library has nothing to build |
| test | `bundle exec ruby -Ilib test/test_calendar.rb`, same prefix |
| run / seed / app\_url | `null` |

Both commands are prefixed with `RB=$(ls -d /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.3.*/x64/bin ... | tail -1); export PATH="${RB:-$(dirname "$(command -v bundle)")}:$PATH"`.

Measured here, from a clean tree, using the strings read back out of the finished manifest:

- install: `Bundle complete! 2 Gemfile dependencies, 16 gems now installed.`
- test: `5 runs, 8 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips` under Ruby 3.3.13
- rubocop: `4 files inspected, no offenses detected`
- control: the test command exits 10 in an empty directory, so it is not passing vacuously
- `bsf sandbox check`: `valid sandbox manifest, tier build_and_test`

## Two things the README's commands did not survive

1. **A bare `bundle install` fails on the runner** with `Bundler::ReadOnlyFileSystemError` against the shared gem home. Fixed by installing into `vendor/bundle`; `/vendor` and `/.bundle` are already in `.gitignore`.
2. **`ruby` and `bundle` are different Ruby installations here.** `bundle` resolves to the tool cache's Ruby 4.0.9 while `ruby` on PATH is `/usr/bin/ruby` 3.3.8, so `bundle exec ruby` died with `Bundler::GemNotFound` listing all 16 gems that had just installed. The PATH prefix puts one Ruby first. It prefers a 3.3.x to match `TargetRubyVersion: 3.3` and CI's `ruby-version: "3.3"` — pinning to bundler's own Ruby also passed, but under a different major from CI, which is the kind of agreement worth keeping.

## Judgement calls worth a second opinion

- **`build` is null rather than `bundle exec rubocop`.** CI's second step does pass, and it does fail in an empty directory, so it would have survived the control check. It is left out because the static gate already runs RuboCop against per-file baselines that tolerate existing offenses, and a bare `rubocop` as the build would be a stricter second copy that disagrees with the gate. Recorded under `dropped` with that reasoning — easy to reverse if the gate's behaviour makes it worthwhile.
- **The install step is the one thing not verified under the trial's own conditions.** Imitating the closed environment with `env -i` and only the six forwarded variables failed at `Errno::ENETUNREACH` to rubygems.org — this setup agent reaches the network only through an egress proxy named in `HTTPS_PROXY`, which the runner does not forward and which does not exist on a GitHub-hosted runner. With the proxy present the same strings pass. If install fails in the trial for a network reason, that is where to look; `rubygems.org` and `index.rubygems.org` are listed under `egress`.

## Context files

Written from reading the repo, with gaps left as gaps rather than filled in:

- **feature-map.md** — `lib/scheduling/` and `test/` are the only two folders of product code. **There is no shared folder**, recorded as absent; the first second-caller sets the precedent.
- **fundamentals.md** — the patterns that recur (raise rather than return false; `ArgumentError` from `initialize`; half-open ranges; rebuild-and-reassign over mutation; a class comment that says *why*) with a file-and-line source on each. Two entries under deliberate exceptions are explicitly marked as **unsourced observations**: the gitignored `Gemfile.lock`, and `Calendar#slots` handing back the live array — the latter is a real wart nobody has written a decision about.
- **history.md** — mostly empty on purpose. No lessons from the product code, no escalations. One verifiable lesson: **PR #5, the earlier attempt to set this factory up, measured `static` and was closed unmerged** — it was designed against a repo that did not yet have the application code, which PR #6 merged one second before #5 was closed.
- **runbook.md** — every command as actually run, with its real output, plus a console snippet under *Verify* for seeing the library work without the test suite (it prints `120`, `["09:00-10:00", "12:00-17:00"]` and `Conflict: 10:30-11:30 clashes with 10:00-11:00`).

## What the sandbox cannot exercise

Listed in full under `capabilities.not_exercised`, with paths: anything needing a process (no executable exists — a change that adds one is the signal to amend); any Ruby or dependency versions other than the day's resolution; time types other than `::Time`, and zone/DST behaviour (`Slot` is duck-typed but every test uses `Time.parse` at a fixed UTC date); concurrency and persistence; and performance — `book` is a linear scan that re-sorts on every insert, and a two-slot suite would not notice that becoming quadratic.

## Research domains

`docs.ruby-lang.org`, `ruby-doc.org`, `docs.seattlerb.org` (minitest), `rubydoc.info`, `docs.rubocop.org`, `bundler.io`, `rubygems.org`.
